cues.text: OK Rosie, shall we try to get some ideas together for our presentation on diet and obesity?
cues.speaker: ADAM

cues.text: Sure.
cues.speaker: ROSIE

cues.text: I can talk about the experiment I did to see if people can tell the difference between real sugar and artificial sweeteners.
cues.speaker: ADAM

cues.text: Where you gave people drinks with either sugar or artificial sweeteners and they had to say which they thought it was?
cues.speaker: ROSIE

cues.text: Yeah. It took me ages to decide exactly how I'd organise it, especially how I could make sure that people didn't know which drink I was giving them.
cues.speaker: ADAM

cues.text: It was hard to keep track of it all, especially as I had so many people doing it - I had to make sure I kept a proper record of what each person had had.
cues.speaker: ADAM

cues.text: So could most people tell the difference?
cues.speaker: ROSIE

cues.text: Yeah - I hadn't thought they would be able to, but most people could.
cues.speaker: ADAM

cues.text: Then there's that experiment I did measuring the fat content of nuts, to see if the nutritional information given on the packet was accurate.
cues.speaker: ROSIE

cues.text: The one where you ground up the nuts and mixed them with a chemical to absorb the fat?
cues.speaker: ADAM

cues.text: Yes. My results were a bit problematic - the fat content for that type of nut seemed much lower than it said on the package.
cues.speaker: ROSIE

cues.text: But I reckon the package information was right.
cues.speaker: ROSIE

cues.text: I think I should probably have ground up the nuts more than I did.
cues.speaker: ROSIE

cues.text: It's possible that the scales for weighing the fat weren't accurate enough, too.
cues.speaker: ROSIE

cues.text: I'd really like to try the experiment again some time.
cues.speaker: ROSIE

cues.text: So what can we say about helping people to lose weight?
cues.speaker: ADAM

cues.text: There's a lot we could say about what restaurants could do to reduce obesity.
cues.speaker: ADAM

cues.text: I read that the items at the start of a menu and the items at the end of a menu are much more likely to be chosen than the items in the middle.
cues.speaker: ADAM

cues.text: So, if you put the low-calorie items at the beginning and end of the menu, people will probably go for the food with fewer calories, without even realising what they're doing.
cues.speaker: ADAM

cues.text: I think food manufacturers could do more to encourage healthy eating.
cues.speaker: ROSIE

cues.text: How?
cues.speaker: ADAM

cues.text: Well, when manufacturers put calorie counts of a food on the label, they're sometimes really confusing and I suspect they do it on purpose.
cues.speaker: ROSIE

cues.text: Because food that's high in calories tastes better, and so they'll sell more.
cues.speaker: ROSIE

cues.text: Yeah, so if you look at the amount of calories in a pizza, they'll give you the calories per quarter pizza and you think, oh that's not too bad.
cues.speaker: ADAM

cues.text: But who's going to eat a quarter pizza?
cues.speaker: ADAM

cues.text: Exactly
cues.speaker: ROSIE

cues.text: I suppose another approach to this problem is to get people to exercise more.
cues.speaker: ADAM

cues.text: Right. In England, the current guidelines are for at least 30 minutes of brisk walking, five days a week.
cues.speaker: ROSIE

cues.text: Now when you ask them, about 40% of men and 30% of women say they do this, but when you objectively measure the amount of walking they do with motion sensors, you find that only 6% of men and 4% of women do the recommended amount of exercise.
cues.speaker: ROSIE

cues.text: Mm, so you can see why obesity is growing.
cues.speaker: ADAM

cues.text: So how can people be encouraged to take more exercise?
cues.speaker: ROSIE

cues.text: Well, for example, think of the location of stairs in a train station.
cues.speaker: ADAM

cues.text: If people reach the stairs before they reach the escalator when they're leaving the station, they're more likely to take the stairs.
cues.speaker: ADAM

cues.text: And if you increase the width of the stairs, you'll get more people using them at the same time.
cues.speaker: ADAM

cues.text: It's an unconscious process and influenced by minor modifications in their environment.
cues.speaker: ADAM

cues.text: Right. And it might not be a big change, but if it happens every day, it all adds up.
cues.speaker: ROSIE

cues.text: Yes. But actually, I'm not sure if we should be talking about exercise in our presentation.
cues.speaker: ADAM

cues.text: Well, we've done quite a bit of reading about it.
cues.speaker: ROSIE

cues.text: I know, but it's going to mean we have a very wide focus, and our tutor did say that we need to focus on causes and solutions in terms of nutrition.
cues.speaker: ADAM

cues.text: I suppose so.
cues.speaker: ROSIE

cues.text: And we've got plenty of information about that.
cues.speaker: ROSIE

cues.text: OK, well that will be simpler.
cues.speaker: ROSIE

cues.text: So what shall we do now?
cues.speaker: ADAM

cues.text: We've still got half an hour before our next lecture.
cues.speaker: ADAM

cues.text: Let's think about what we're going to include and what will go where.
cues.speaker: ROSIE

cues.text: Then we can decide what slides we need.
cues.speaker: ROSIE

cues.text: OK, fine.
cues.speaker: ADAM
